instruction: Determine the names of the mountains in three pictures from my Pictures folder, copy them to a new 'Mountains' folder on the Desktop, and rename each copied photo after its respective mountain.

metadata.explanation: Task requires identifying 3 mountain images, creating a Desktop/Mountains folder, and copying files with mountain names. The evaluator uses PIL-based SHA256 hashes to verify correct files were copied with acceptable mountain names. Verified hashes using PIL (img.tobytes()): picture1.jpg=ec076282...(Kilimanjaro), picture2.jpg=6ed4239e...(Everest), picture3.jpg=79f45d40...(Mount Hua). Similar complexity to original task (identify + file operation) but involves copying to new location instead of renaming in place. Partial credit: score = (correct copies) / 3.
metadata.scoring_breakdown: 0.33 per correctly copied and named mountain image

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator semantically verifies all instruction requirements: (1) identifies correct mountain images via PIL-based SHA256 hashing, (2) verifies files were copied to /home/user/Desktop/Mountains destination, (3) validates renaming with comprehensive acceptable name variants per mountain
Hash-based verification is robust - ensures correct images were copied, not just arbitrary files with correct names
Getter logic correctly extracts destination folder contents and computes PIL image hashes matching expected hash format
Metric comparison logic properly checks hash presence and filename matching against acceptable variants
Partial credit scoring (correct_count / 3) is semantically appropriate for multi-image task
Expected values are well-defined with verified PIL hashes and comprehensive name variants (Kilimanjaro/Kili, Everest/Sagarmatha/Chomolungma, Mount Hua/Huashan)
Edge cases handled: returns 0.0 for missing results/expected, logs mismatches for debugging
No UI state dependencies - pure filesystem verification works correctly post-execution
Metric parameter handling is correct: accesses expected.get('expected', {}) to retrieve hash mappings from rules dictionary
